headline: Sangrur: 72 fire detections on 31 October
briefing: On 31 October 2025, satellites detected 72 fires in Sangrur district, releasing 421.3 MW of fire radiative power. That is 169.5% above the 7-day average of 26.7. Sangrur ranks number 1 in Punjab, which recorded 273 detections in total. The nearest city, Patiala, has a forecast median PM2.5 of 90.8 µg/m³ for 1 November 2025, with an 80% interval of 54.4 to 103.2. The median is above the national 24-hour standard of 60 µg/m³. Wind at Patiala blows from the NW (322.0°) at 8.1 km/h, with the largest upwind fire shares from Outside Punjab (23.1%) and Sangrur (22.3%). On the 2024 and 2025 test seasons the model's average error here was 10.5 µg/m³, against 10.1 for persistence, so it did not beat that simple baseline. Limitation: satellites detect heat anomalies, not stubble burning itself, and miss fires under cloud, so counts are lower bounds; PM2.5 here is modelled, not measured. [K035]

results.title: Limitations of this project
results.text:
# What to keep in mind when reading any output

**Fires.** Satellites detect heat anomalies. They do not know that a fire is stubble burning. They miss fires that burn between overpasses, fires under cloud, and small or short burns. A district's detection count is a lower bound. Fire dates are UTC dates that we treat as local days, so some night detections are filed one day early.

**Air quality.** PM2.5 is modelled by CAMS on a coarse grid. It is not measured at street level and it is not CPCB monitor data. It already includes fire emissions as the model sees them.

**Districts.** We use 22 district boundaries. Malerkotla, created in 2021, is not a separate district in our boundary data. Its area is counted in Sangrur.
